newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay index shares in bull run, index up 1.81 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bombay index shares in bull run, index up 1.81 pct.

text.p: ** (1005 GMT) - Bombay benchmark index sweeps through
4,500 mark to close 80.93 pts, or 1.81 pct higher, at a
provisional 4,546.30
** Hindustan Lever 1997 first half results slightly
above expectations, traders say; firm posts net at 2.56
billion rupees against 1.85 billion in year-ago period
** Traders expect market to take a strike at its 4,600 peak
on renewed investment demand in small cap stocks and
sustained fund buying in top index stocks
** Castrol and Ponds due to announce results
** National Stock Exchange index up 22.50 pts at 1,272.90
A flurry of buying orders powered Bombay shares higher on Tuesday to drive the benchmark 30-share index through the psychological barrier of 4,500 in hectic trade, dealers said.
The market outlook stayed bullish despite some concerns about profit-taking at higher levels, they said.
"The investor has turned back to the markets. The bull run should continue," said Kirti Doshi, dealer at local brokers Biyani Securites.
An impressive first half performance by multinational firm Hindustan Lever aided market sentiment, traders said.

Hindustan Lever, the Indian subsidiary of Anglo-Dutch conglomerate Unilever Plc said on Tuesday its net profit in the six months to June 30 totalled 2.56 billion rupees -- slightly higher than expected by analysts -- on sales of 38.9 billion rupees.
Lower interest costs and tax rates boosted Hindustan Lever results and analysts said they expect the multinational firm to maintain the momentum for the whole year.
"We're forecasting 20 percent top-line growth for 1997 and bottomline growth of 27 percent," an analyst at Peregrine Capital India said.
Shares of the multinational firm ended 17.50 rupees higher at 1,533 at the Bombay Stock Exchange.
The net profit and sales in the first half of 1996 were 18.5 billion rupees and 32.8 billion respectively, but these were before a merger with affiliate Brooke Bond Lipton India Ltd was completed.
In the first six months to June 30, interest costs fell 35.4 percent to 184.0 million rupees from 284.8 million in the year-ago period, the firm said.
Castrol India Ltd and Ponds Ltd had not announced results by the close of market hours on Tuesday.
-- Anshuman Daga, Bombay equities desk +91-22-265 9000
